segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ כּוֹפִין אֶת הַסַּל לִפְנֵי הָאֶפְרוֹחִים כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלוּ וְיֵרְדוּ. תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת שֶׁבָּרְחָה — דּוֹחִין אוֹתָהּ עַד שֶׁתִּכָּנֵס.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One may overturn a basket in front of the chicks» so that «they can climb on and climb off» of it. Likewise, with regard to «a hen that fled» that one seeks to retrieve, «one may push it» even with his hands «until it reenters» the house.

segments.he: מְדַדִּין עֲגָלִין וּסְיָיחִין. אִשָּׁה מְדַדָּה אֶת בְּנָהּ. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֵימָתַי — בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֵל אַחַת וּמַנִּיחַ אַחַת, אֲבָל אִם הָיָה גּוֹרֵר — אָסוּר.
segments.en: «One may help calves and foals to walk,» and likewise «a woman may help her son to walk. Rabbi Yehuda said: When» is it permitted? «When» her son «picks one» foot «up and puts one» foot «down» by himself. «However, if» her son «were dragging» both his feet, «it would be prohibited» because it would be like carrying him in the public domain.

moves.summary: One may overturn a basket for chicks and push a fleeing hen
One may help calves, foals and a child walk
Only when the child lifts his own feet; dragging is forbidden
moves.about: helping a child walk is permitted only when the child steps by himself, not when dragged
